clusters.name: Walter's move to Sorrel Valley, 1952–1953
clusters.reason: Around Walter's move across the country in March 1952 and the purchase of the orchard, within the year: June became homesick and wrote to her sister Edna daily, then kept to her bed for weeks; Walter spent long hours in the trees away from June; Glen got into fights at his new school; Walter stopped writing to his brother Harlan after a quarrel over their father's land money; Walter and June rowed over money for new trees. By September 1953 June had joined the church choir and her letters to Edna thinned out, and the period settles there.

clusters.name: Walter's orchard failed, 1968–1969
clusters.reason: Around the orchard's failure in May 1968 when the late frost took the whole crop and the bank called in the loan, within months: Walter drank heavily most nights and he and Glen blamed each other for the loan; Glen and Marian took over the family's money and talks with the bank; Glen's son Carl developed worse asthma attacks that winter; by April 1969 Nora began wetting the bed. By October 1969 Walter stopped drinking and took work pruning other men's trees, and the period settles.

clusters.name: Glen's job lost at the cannery, 1975–1976
clusters.reason: Around Glen's loss of his job when the Ridgeport cannery closed in February 1975, within the year: Glen sat out of work in the truck in the yard for hours; he and Marian fought loud at night over money; Marian took a second job cleaning offices at night; Nora stopped eating properly and lost weight; Nora kept to her room and distanced from her mother; Walter drank again after six years without it. By June 1976, when Glen started driving a delivery truck and Nora was eating again and had made the track team, the period settles.

clusters.name: Wilma moved into Nora and Sam's house, 1990–1991
clusters.reason: Around Wilma moving into Nora and Sam's house in January 1990, within months: Nora clashed with Wilma over the children's bedtimes and meals; Sam worked late and kept out of the kitchen rows while taking his mother's side; Owen had tantrums at preschool; Wilma took over Lily's care; Nora's eczema flared on both hands; Nora and Sam rowed most nights; Marian drove over twice a week to take Nora's side. By June 1991 Wilma took a flat in town, and by August 1991 Nora's eczema had cleared over the summer, and the period settles.

declined.reason: 1994-08-12 to 1994-08-16: Four days from the wildfire coming over the ridge to the family being allowed home with the house untouched, everyone calm again within the week. An acute episode around a real threat, not a period.

1996-10-15 to 1997-06-15: Tess's drinking began in October 1996; Nora's shifts toward her sister and Marian's overfunctioning are in the same months, but no change in who is in the family or in how a key member functions sits on a known date among these events, so there is not enough in the diagram to choose a reading.
